newsitem.title: UK: European stocks surge, Frankfurt ends at record.
newsitem.headline: European stocks surge, Frankfurt ends at record.

text.p: European stock markets climbed sharply Friday with Frankfurt propelled to a record close as a stronger dollar boosted prospects for German exporters.
Paris stocks finished at their highest level of the year as investors hoped for a speedy end to the French truckers' strike and drew comfort from the dollar's gains and higher bond prices.
On currency markets the dollar rose against the German mark as traders fretted about growing tension between France and Germany over exchange rates and monetary policy.
In Frankfurt, shares ended a record-breaking week by closing at a record 2,845.52 points on the DAX index, up 28.03 points, and making a gain of 3 percent in just one week.
"The dynamism of the current climb had been surprising," said Peter Pietsch, economist at Germany's Commerzbank.

The market was driven by a combination of strength in German government bonds, which have reached record highs, and the stronger dollar, which benefits German exporters, particularly the chemical industry.

In Paris, stocks soared as high as 1.4 percent to 2,327.81 on the blue-chip CAC-40, eclipsing the previous intra-day high for 1996 of 2,295.54 and edging closer to its record of 2,360.98 set in February 1994. The CAC-40 index finished up 25.35 at 2,315.66.
"The bourse is feeling very bullish," a trader said, amid signs of optimism over the 12-day-old truckers' dispute.
The strike by drivers blockading the country neared conclusion Friday after unions signed an early retirement deal and consulted their members at roadblocks on ending the action.

The sparkling performances in Paris and Frankfurt was largely thanks to the strengthening dollar. It was lifted again by Bank of France monetary policy council member Jean-Pierre Gerard when he said on Thursday he favoured a stronger dollar against the mark.
One way to drive the dollar higher would be to tempt dollar investors by cutting short-term interest rates in France and Germany, making stocks more attractive there.
In London, suffering from the stronger British pound, stocks climbed cautiously after Thursday's late rally sparked by renewed bid speculation.
The pound soared to a 33-month peak against the mark as a rise in British interest rate looked increasingly likely to staunch inflationary pressures. It was at 2.5821 marks and $1.6845 at one point.
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 7.8 points higher at 4,058.0.
